correctness.rationale: The relevant vanishing first-order bracket is the cross-bracket; each diagonal bracket is n. Conditional on the fair coefficient bits, the predictable cross factor is the displayed sign. The mod-2 Pascal matrix has unit diagonal, so the scenery is iid fair and independent of the walk. A completed level contributes H_j f_j with iid geometric holds of mean 2 and variance 2; the unfinished hold and initial convention give the stated remainder. For each integer T, a union bound and Hoeffding over O_T(n²) scenery intervals of length at most n^(2/3) is summable at every fixed positive threshold times √n. The clock deviation is uniformly O_P(√n), so replacing the scenery index by ⌊nt/2⌋ costs o_P(√n) for almost every scenery. The maximal hold up to Tn has geometric-tail control. The centered independent rewards f_j(H_j−2) meet functional Lindeberg uniformly in the signs; at the level time nt/2 their variance rate in physical time is 1. The uniform clock law and continuity of the limit justify the time change regardless of dependence. Conditional convergence to the same law gives joint asymptotic independence from the environmental centering by bounded-continuous product tests and dominated convergence, adding variance rate 2. The scenery LIL forces unbounded positive and negative center shifts, so the uncentered scalar quenched laws are not tight. For a direct variance check, in the alternate initial convention the annealed covariance of terms k steps apart is 2^(−k), giving variance 3n−4+4·2^(−n). The deterministic-index centered reward and center also give the stated leading variance split in L²: on the n^(2/3) clock window, the centered-reward maximal squared error is O(n^(2/3)) by the martingale maximal inequality; outside it, fourth-moment bounds and the binomial tail make the squared error o(n). Jointly the scenery replacement has squared error E|M_n−⌊n/2⌋|=O(√n), and the residual squared error is O(log² n). The finite attached checks are not used as evidence for convergence.

value.rationale: A first-order orthogonality result does not tell whether a fixed typical environment yields stable second-order behavior. The explicit centering and contrasting annealed limit give a useful answer in a canonical fair bootstrap, including a quantitative separation of environmental and conditional fluctuations. The uncentered quenched non-tightness is a substantive distinction rather than another variance calculation.
